passages.text: But none of us can suffer anything of this kind. Rather, they are themselves punished by us when, after entering someone, they beg us to let them come out slowly. But perhaps someone will say, “Some who revere God also fall into such afflictions.” I say that this is impossible. For the God-revering person is the one I mean, the one who truly reveres God, not someone merely called so. The one who truly is such carries out the commands of the law given him. If someone acts impiously, he is not reverent. In the same way, if a foreigner practices the law, he is a Jew; a Jew who does not practice it is a Greek. For the person who believes God practices the law, and through this faith also removes the other afflictions that resemble mountains and weigh him down. But the person who does not practice the law plainly deserts his post because he does not believe God. Thus, as a sinner who is not a Jew, because of sin he is overpowered by the afflictions appointed to punish sinners. By God’s will, determined from the beginning, punishment justly follows those who revere him on account of their transgressions. This happens so that, after exacting the sin like a debt through torment, it may present those who have turned back clean at the judgment of all. For just as luxury here becomes for the wicked a loss of eternal good things, so punishments are sent to Jews who transgress as an exaction, so that, after receiving the due for their transgression here, they may be released from the eternal punishment there.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they beg us to let them come out slowly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes us as the object of beg and demons as the implied subject of coming out. Permission is implicit. Beg us to withdraw slowly is another grammatical grouping, but the expulsion context favors the former.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a Jew who does not practice it is a Greek
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the author’s explicit Jew/Greek categories defined here through observance. Greek can function as Gentile in the religious argument; no literal change of ancestry is added.
Keeps the turning verb distinct from μετανοέω/reorient.
Retains the debt-collection image of punishment.

passages.text: But you cannot say these things, for you do not believe that things there are as we say—I mean the place where everyone receives repayment. Therefore, ignorant of what benefits you, you are ambushed by temporary pleasures so as not to receive eternal things. We therefore try to demonstrate what benefits you, so that, fully assured about the promises of reverence toward God, through good actions you may be able to inherit with us the age without sorrow. Until you come to know us, then, do not be angry with us as though we were lying about the good things we want for you. For we have not begrudged bringing you what we consider true and good; on the contrary, we have been eager to make you fellow heirs of the good things we believe in. For this is how one must speak to unbelievers. But that we really speak truth about what we say you will not be able to know unless you first obey with a love of truth.

lexical_decisions.chosen: obey with a love of truth
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπακούω can be listen or obey; obey retains the demanded response while the adverb retains love of truth.

passages.text: For the present, therefore, even if the serpent lurking within you wishes to ambush you in countless ways, putting evil thoughts and distractions into you, you must contend against him all the more in this way: listen to us continually. For you who have been so greatly deceived must sit together and learn how to chant against him. Otherwise it is impossible. By chanting against him, I mean resisting his evil counsels with reason, remembering that from the beginning he brought death into the world through a promise of knowledge.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the incantation metaphor that the author immediately defines as rational resistance, not a newly supplied magical formula.

passages.text: Therefore the prophet of truth, knowing that the world was greatly deceived and seeing that it had agreed with evil, did not love peace with it, since that peace arose from error. Setting out that it ultimately brings death upon all who agree with evil, in place of error he cast into those who had become clear-minded an anger against the one who had ambushed them, like fire and resembling a sword. Holding out the word, he does away with ignorance through knowledge, as though cutting and separating the living from the dead. So, as evil was overcome by knowledge in accordance with the law, war gripped everything. For the sake of salvation a son who yielded separated from a disobedient father, or a father from a child, or a mother from a daughter, or a daughter from a mother—in short, relatives from relatives and friends from companions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅτι εἰς τέλος ἐπιφέρει πᾶσιν τοῖς πρὸς κακίαν ὁμογνωμονοῦσιν παραθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Setting out that it ultimately brings death upon all who agree with evil
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object brought is implicit. Death is inferred from the end of 11.18 and the ensuing living/dead contrast. The it can be the peace founded on error or its sustaining error; no new punishment is specified.
The recipient of yielding is not explicit. The saving instruction is contextual, but the English does not insert that recipient.

source_issues.source_quote: ὅτι εἰς τέλος ἐπιφέρει πᾶσιν τοῖς πρὸς κακίαν ὁμογνωμονοῦσιν παραθεὶς
source_issues.issue: The object of brings upon is implicit. Death in the main text is inferred from the immediately preceding death-language and ensuing living/dead contrast. The antecedent can be error-based peace or its sustaining error.

passages.text: And let no one say, “How is this just, for parents to be separated from children and children from parents?” It is entirely just. For if by staying with them they not only did them no good but also perished with them, how is it not just for the one who wants to be saved to be separated from the one who does not want this but wishes them to perish together? Moreover, those who had understood what is better did not themselves want to be separated, but to remain with them and benefit them by teaching better things. Therefore the disobedient, unwilling to listen to them, themselves fought against them, separating from them, persecuting them, and hating them. But those who suffered these things pitied them as people ambushed by ignorance and, taught to understand, prayed for those who mistreated them, having learned that ignorance is the cause of sin. For the teacher himself, when nailed up, prayed to the Father that the sin of those killing him might be forgiven, saying, “Father, forgive them their sins, for they do not know what they are doing.” Becoming imitators of the teacher themselves, in their sufferings they prayed for those who inflicted them, as they had been taught. Thus they did not separate because they hated their parents, since they even offered prayers for those who were not their parents but had become enemies, and try to love them as they were commanded.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative connects instruction in understanding with the prayerful response, not with a newly supplied revelation.
Bracketed letters are already supplied by the selected edition; no new restoration has been made.
Follows the supplied bracketed reading and preserves the contrast with enemies.
